title: Long-run exact-shape launch and projection optimization campaign

acceptance_criteria.AC-WF-1: The workflow validates with zero errors and every executed test, profile, benchmark, candidate, and closure gate has an immutable Campaign 6 attempt record.
acceptance_criteria.AC-BASE-1: The Campaign 5 fingerprint, protected organizer inputs, environment, complete final matrix, and target profiles are freshly verified before candidate changes.
acceptance_criteria.AC-CORRECT-1: Every retained candidate has zero failed elements and no unauthorized fallback, error, OOM, or skip in all affected correctness gates.
acceptance_criteria.AC-PERF-1: A retained candidate improves complete-matrix geomean by approximately five percent or provides a reproducible target-latency, kernel-time, memory, or launch benefit of about five percent, with no required case regressing more than two percent absent an explicit reviewed exception.
acceptance_criteria.AC-EVIDENCE-1: Raw samples, latency summaries, error counts, backend counts, profiler events, memory, environment, source hashes, implementation fingerprint, and command wall time are tied to the exact candidate.
acceptance_criteria.AC-BOUNDARY-1: Any launch or dispatch rule is exact-shape or demonstrably safe at adjacent affected shapes and leaves unmeasured shapes on the previously validated policy.
acceptance_criteria.AC-REVIEW-1: A surviving candidate receives an independent provenance, correctness, performance, boundary, and maintainability review before integration.
acceptance_criteria.AC-RELEASE-1: Only an approved winner is retained and final, organizer-default, held-out, source-derived, profile, test, documentation, workflow, graph, and working-tree gates are current.

roles.why: Normalizes the requested long campaign into measurable bounded loops
Owns sequencing, isolation, evidence lineage, integration, and stop rules
Separates exact-row launch and projection hypotheses into independently reversible work
Ranks fresh target profiles and calculates the end-to-end ceiling
Implements one narrow kernel launch or projection candidate at a time
Measures strict accuracy, target latency, distributions, memory, and actual backend execution
Challenges overfitting, provenance, numerical safety, and timing credibility
Issues the final retain, reject, plateau, or hold decision

tasks.title: Freeze and validate Campaign 6 scope and baseline identity
Run fresh final baseline and exact row 6, row 7, row 8, and row 11 profiles
Tune exact row-6 huge-batch head-32 launch geometry
Tune exact row-7 and preserve row-11 padded-width head-8 launch geometry
Recheck one profile-authorized wide-model projection candidate
validation: strict state dict and cache tests

tasks.title: Test untried exact row-11 padded-width query-tile and warp variants
Review every surviving candidate and the composite
Retain only approved winners and regenerate complete evidence
Perform source-of-truth, workflow, graph, and scoped-tree closure

loops.finding_condition: A row-6 launch candidate fails correctness, target timing, profiler, boundary, or provenance gates
loops.acceptance_condition: One exact-row launch is reproducibly faster and fully correct, or five variants establish a plateau

loops.finding_condition: A padded-width launch candidate fails row-7 accuracy, row-11 protection, stress, timing, profile, or provenance gates
loops.acceptance_condition: One exact-row launch is reproducibly faster with all width-eight gates clean, or five variants establish a plateau

loops.finding_condition: The wide-model projection candidate is neutral, slower, inaccurate, or changes unsupported behavior
loops.acceptance_condition: A reproducible end-to-end and profile benefit clears all row-8 and neighbor gates, or the measured projection surface is closed as plateaued

loops.finding_condition: An untried row-11 query-tile or warp candidate fails correctness, row-7 protection, long-sample timing, profile, or provenance gates
loops.acceptance_condition: One exact-row launch is reproducibly faster with all width-eight gates clean, or three new-axis variants establish a plateau
